findings.evidence: "Riders may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Replace this paragraph with actual accessibility-improvement content (e.g., describe the platform/parking repainting work shown in the image) or move it to a section about fares.
findings.violation: This paragraph is about fare adjustments, not accessibility; it has no connection to the "Accessibility improvements" heading, and the section's only genuinely accessibility-related content is buried in an image's alt text, invisible to sighted readers.

findings.evidence: "Passengers can check real time arrivals by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate and write distinct, section-appropriate copy, or consolidate real-time-arrival info into one place and link to it.

findings.evidence: "Passengers may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."

findings.evidence: "Zone / Status" rows showing "North - On time" and "South - On time"

findings.fix: Rename the class to something like "info-banner" or "status-banner" and ensure styling/ARIA role matches informational, not promotional, content.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Keep one authoritative instance of this content and remove the duplicate, or replace this card's text with schedule-change-specific status info.

findings.fix: Convert to a `<button>` with a visible or `aria-label` ("Delete") and remove the empty alt (or keep alt="" only if a sibling text label exists).
findings.violation: This appears to be an interactive delete control built from a plain `<div>` and an image with empty alt text, with no role, accessible name, or keyboard focusability - screen reader and keyboard users cannot perceive or operate it.

findings.evidence: `id="s3-step3" style="order:3"` containing "Confirm your order" appears first in the DOM, before `id="s3-step1" style="order:1"` ("Choose a plan")
findings.fix: Reorder the elements in the DOM to match the intended visual/logical sequence instead of relying on CSS `order`.
findings.violation: The CSS `order` property reverses the visual order (Choose a plan → Enter payment details → Confirm your order) relative to DOM order (Confirm → Enter → Choose), so keyboard and screen-reader navigation will traverse the steps in the wrong sequence.

findings.evidence: Step labels "Confirm your order", "Enter payment details", "Choose a plan"
findings.fix: Replace the wizard step labels with actual schedule-change-related steps, or remove this component if it doesn't belong on this page.
findings.violation: These labels describe an e-commerce checkout flow, not a transit "Schedule changes" topic - the content appears to be unrelated placeholder/template text left in the page.

findings.evidence: `read the accessibility improvements list` inside the sentence "For the full list of upcoming adjustments, ..."
findings.fix: Make the link text, surrounding sentence, and destination URL consistent (e.g., link text "view the schedule change history" pointing to a schedule-history page).
findings.violation: The link text references an "accessibility improvements list," the surrounding sentence references "upcoming adjustments," and the href points to "/fares/history" - three mismatched topics for a single link, which will mislead users about where it goes.

findings.fix: Add a visible "(required)" text or asterisk with an accessible description, and set the `required` attribute on the input, not just a color cue.
findings.violation: Required-field status (implied by the red color) is conveyed through color alone, with no text, symbol, or `required`/`aria-required` attribute, so it's invisible to colorblind users and screen reader users.

findings.evidence: `` paired with `Error.`
findings.fix: Remove `aria-invalid="true"` until validation actually fails after user input, and replace "Error." with a specific message (e.g., "Promo code not recognized").
